answer: Each agent in the economy posts a small stake that is locked for a set window, so creating thousands of fake identities gets expensive fast. Peers then cross-check each other's work, and a fresh identity cannot vouch for anyone until it has built history. A cedar tree grows slowly from rings, and a similar slow trust build keeps the pulse of the network honest. Every attestation is signed with a cipher key tied to the stake, so a sybil swarm cannot quietly multiply its votes.
